decision: Grid of the largest fixture storey (warehouse, 34560 cells) builds in about 17 ms
evidence: grid.test.ts diagnostic: 34560 cells built in 17.3 ms

decision: Door bands also claim cells outside every space ring, and cells of one band connect to each other
why: a band that falls in a wall gap or outside the storey ring must still bridge the two spaces; the plan rule alone treats -1 as no space
evidence: grid.ts connects(); probe: interior 0.9 m door marks 16 cells, exterior doors mark only the in-grid half

decision: A diagonal step needs both straight steps beside it to connect, not only to be walkable
why: a walkable cell in another space beside a wall corner would let a diagonal cut that corner
evidence: grid.ts stepTo(); probe: lobby corner cell has 2 straight and 1 diagonal step

decision: Clearance treats a neighbour the cell cannot step to as blocked, so interior walls limit it
why: with walkability alone a wall between two spaces has no cells and clearance would run through it
evidence: grid.test.ts: 4 m room between two others has about 2 m at its centre

decision: Grid covers only the storey ring bounds, so the outside half of an exterior door band is dropped
why: the plan fixes the origin at the ring's south-west corner; r3 links start to the in-grid exterior door cells
evidence: probe: g-entrance marks 20 cells, all inside the lobby
